title: Remove one concrete barrier from a piece of everyday information

sections.title: Understand the distinction
sections.body: Accessible information makes required facts available through a workable mode; a clear-looking artifact can still have a bad reading order or an unconfirmed physical route.

sections.title: Complete fictional practice material
sections.body: Fresh notice facts: map discussion Friday 11:00–11:30, Room D; materials supplied; questions accepted by text through the organizer or in person. Step-free room access is not confirmed. Flawed draft image reads “Friday, usual room, bring supplies”; its text alternative says only “event poster.” The author controls both versions.

sections.title: Work through the supplied case
sections.body: Write a complete ordinary-text notice and useful text alternative. Name the unverified access fact and a short reading-order check rather than claiming universal compliance.

sections.title: Try a different case before checking
sections.body: A notice puts a cancellation only in red text with no words identifying its status. What should change?

checks.title: Compare reasoning and review the supplied result
checks.body: Preserve Friday 11:00–11:30, Room D, supplied materials, both question routes and unconfirmed step-free access. The alternative needs the essential content, not “poster.” Later fiction: a reader receives place before time but can identify all facts; this is one usable result, not universal accessibility. Partial: fix text but leave an empty alternative. Incorrect: advertise step-free access without confirmation.
criteria: All required facts survive the format change
Meaning is not carried by color or image alone

checks.title: Check the changed case
checks.body: Express cancellation in words with the affected event/date and any verified next step; color may supplement but cannot be the sole carrier of the essential distinction.
